links.outcome: Documentation time per note and clinician stress after AI scribe deployment
links.effect: Estimated documentation time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes (-29%, p = 1.70e-11); ability to work without administrative stress rose from 2.41 to 3.14 (p = 2.46e-8).
links.quote: With the introduction of the AI medical scribe, the estimated time spent on documentation per note decreased from 6.69 minutes to 4.72 minutes (-29%, p = 1.70e-11).

links.outcome: Local ambient scribe assessment of usability, clinician well-being, and time savings
links.effect: Documentation time per note decreased 29%; stress-free work rose from 2.41 to 3.14; presence with patients rose from 3.73 to 4.33; median editing time 93 seconds.
links.quote: On a five-point Likert scale, the ability to work without stress related to administrative tasks increased from a mean of 2.41 to 3.14 (p = 2.46e-8), and perceived presence with patients increased from 3.73 to 4.33 (p = 2.47e-8).

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world deployment of an AI medical scribe across a European health system, measuring documentation time and clinician experience, but does not compare specific deployment practices or guardrails.
